sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Shift in Goal**: The INC officially abandoned the demand for **Dominion Status** (as proposed in the Nehru Report) in favor of **Purna Swaraj** (Complete Independence).
• **Leadership Dynamics**: **Jawaharlal Nehru** was elected President, symbolizing the rise of the younger, radical wing of the Congress over the older, moderate leadership.
• **Legislative Boycott**: The session mandated the **boycott of the Round Table Conference** and authorized the Working Committee to launch a **Civil Disobedience Movement**.
• **Symbolic Action**: It was decided that **January 26, 1930**, would be observed as the first Independence Day across India.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: From Dominion Status to Purna Swaraj
Failure of British to accept Nehru Report within one-year deadline
Lack of British commitment to self-rule

items.definition: Complete Independence, implying total severance of ties with the British Empire, distinct from the limited self-governance of Dominion Status.
A strategy of non-violent resistance involving the deliberate violation of specific laws to challenge the legitimacy of colonial authority.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Independence Pledge**: The resolution authorized the Congress Working Committee to launch a program of civil disobedience including non-payment of taxes.
• **Flag Hoisting**: Nehru hoisted the tricolor flag on the banks of the Ravi River at midnight on December 31, 1929.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Internal Dissent**: Balancing the radical demands of the youth wing with the cautious approach of Gandhi and the old guard.
• **British Response**: The session set the stage for the Dandi March (1930) as the practical application of the Lahore mandate.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'L-P-R' (Lahore, Purna Swaraj, Ravi).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Lahore Session (1929) declared Purna Swaraj on the banks of the Ravi River.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses the 'Independence Day' date (Jan 26, 1930) with the actual date of the session (Dec 1929). Also, note that the INC did not demand 'Complete Independence' in the 1928 Calcutta session; they gave the British one year to accept Dominion Status.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Radicalization of the National Movement' to describe the transition from the 1928 Nehru Report to the 1929 Lahore Resolution.

keyTakeaways: The Lahore Session marked the formal end of the 'Dominion Status' era.
It empowered the Congress to initiate the Civil Disobedience Movement.
The choice of January 26 as Independence Day provided the historical rationale for choosing the same date for the commencement of the Indian Constitution in 1950.
